title: Structure of valid verifier inputs
statement: Let $z$ be a bit string satisfying the validity guard. Write $Y$ for its instance part and $W$ for its certificate part; write $\alpha$, $x$, $1^n$, and $1^t$ for the code, input, width, and clock fields extracted from $Y$, respectively, with $n$ and $t$ the lengths of the width and clock fields. Then $z=YW$, the length of $W$ is one more than the length of $Y$, and $Y=\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle$.
replaced: For a bit string $z$, write $s(z)$ for its odd split (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), $\pi_1, \pi_2$ for the two components of a pair encoding (the empty word when parsing fails), $Y = \pi_1(s(z))$ and $W = \pi_2(s(z))$; the code, input, width and clock fields of $z$ are $\pi_1(Y)$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(Y))$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$. The guard $G(z)$ holds when $s(z)$, $Y$, $\pi_2(Y)$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(Y))$ all parse as pair encodings and the width and clock fields consist only of ones. If $G(z)$ holds, then $z = YW$, $|W| = |Y| + 1$, and $Y = \langle \alpha, \langle x, \langle 1^n, 1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $\alpha$ and $x$ are the code and input fields, $n$ and $t$ are the lengths of the width and clock fields, and $1^k$ is the word of $k$ ones.
